newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shares end lower in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shares end lower in quiet trading.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended lower after a day of quiet trading in which leading shares showed little upside potential, dealers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell 0.20 percent to end at 18,044.75 on a trading volume of about 4.0 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB index slipped 0.17 percent, meanwhile, ending the day at 1,186.69 on a volume of about 1.0 billion pesos.
"The market was very quiet and weak," one Bogota-based broker said of the lackluster session in which he said price action was essentially "stagnant."

He and others said they had expected manufacturing and textile companies to get a lift from Tuesday night's congressional approval of a law designed to crack down on the country's booming trade in contraband goods. But no such rise was evident in trading Wedneday.

Losers included Compania Nacional de Chocolates of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, which closed 0.51 percent lower in Medellin at 9,750 pesos per share. Blue-chip brewing giant Bavaria also ended lower, shedding 0.64 percent in Medellin to close at 7,849.49 pesos a share.
